title: Associations Between the MMPI-3 Personality Disorder Syndrome Scales and Normal-Range Personality Traits
titleZh: MMPI-3人格障碍综合征量表与常模范围人格特质的关联
abstract: This study examines the associations between the recently developed personality disorder (PD) syndrome scales for the Minnesota Multiphasic Personality Inventory-3 (MMPI-3) and the Multidimensional Personality Questionnaire (MPQ), a normal-range measure of personality. We aimed to extend the construct validity findings for these scales by examining associations in both a college student sample ( n = 824) and a public safety preemployment sample ( n = 2,895) to evaluate the generalizability of our findings across age, gender, and levels of pathology. Overall, we observed that the correlations between the personality pathology constructs measured by the MMPI-3 PD Syndrome scales and the normal-range personality constructs measured by the MPQ were very similar across the two groups, evidenced by consistent patterns of significant associations. Our hypothesized associations between the two instruments were largely supported, with some noteworthy exceptions, which we discuss. These findings support the conceptualization of personality disorders as manifesting at the extremes of normal-range personality constructs and that a dimensional structure likely (imperfectly) underlies both normal- and abnormal-range personality. Implications and recommendations for future research are also discussed.
